title: Digital engineering technician
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Support digital engineers and specialists in completing complex tasks using digital engineering techniques.
ssa1: 5 Construction, Planning and the Built Environment

knowledges.detail: Health and safety regulations and procedures, relevant to the industry, occupation and responsibilities.
The implications of poor health, safety and welfare performance.
Principles and techniques of identifying, recording and tracking health and safety risks to safe working practices.
Environmental and sustainability regulations, legislation, standards and guidance.
Sustainability principles and techniques.
Engineering regulations, legislation, codes, standards, policies and strategies that impact the industry and support the delivery of operational requirements.
Established and emerging technology within the industry.
Planning, prioritising, work scheduling and time management techniques.
The life cycle of construction project and how this relates to digital engineering.
Financial and contractual obligations in construction projects.
Principles and techniques of quantification and costings within a digital environment.
Design Process: Principles, practices and management.
Roles and responsibilities within the construction industry, how they relate to one another and where your organisation sits.
The purpose of their role within the organisation, including their level of responsibility, accountability and when to escalate tasks and issues and to whom.
Information technology and digital systems used to support digital engineering operations. General data protection regulation (GDPR). Cyber security.
Quality assurance procedures and monitoring processes during the life cycle of the built asset.
Organisational and client objectives, requirements and value; Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key performance indicators (KPI’s).
Collaborative working techniques with internal and external stakeholders including own team members and the exchanging of information.

Verbal and written communication techniques. Giving and receiving information. Adapting style to audience. Plain English principles. Barriers in communication and how to overcome them. Specific terminology
Types, quality and ethical data analysis techniques.

Principles of ISO 19650 – managing information with building information modelling (BIM) including BIM execution plans (BEP), capability and capacity assessment (CCA), master information delivery plan (MIDPs) and Task information delivery plans (TIDPs).
Information and documentation for open-format information exchange for example Industry foundation class (IFC), construction organisation building information exchange (COBie).
Principles of model federation and clash detection.
Principles and practices of digital information model checks and data validation.
Principles and practices of a common data environment (CDE).
3D, 4D (time) and 5D (cost) modelling: Principles, benefits, practices and techniques.
Principles and techniques of reality capture technology and data. Photogrammetry, drones, laser scanning, GPR, LIDAR, Point cloud (data).
Public source data: Ordinance Survey data, open maps. national LIDAR programme. National Underground Asset Register (NUAR).
Asset legacy information: how it is obtained and managed.
Principles of developing information to support management of the asset throughout the whole lifecycle.
Problem solving tools and techniques.
Methods of interpreting and extracting information for example health and safety information, manufacturer's instructions, drawings, plans, specifications or reports.
Principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace. Unconscious bias.
Sources of continuing professional development (planned and unplanned) and recording methods.
Personal wellbeing and mental health awareness.

behaviours.detail: Take responsibility for own obligations for health, safety and welfare issues.
Act professionally, considers their organisation's operational, ethical, safety and sustainability priorities.
Contributes to equity, diversity, and inclusivity workplace culture.
Recognise limitations, seek input from others and escalate issues when required.
Collaborate within teams, across disciplines and with internal and external stakeholders.
Respond and adapt to work demands and situations.
Committed to maintaining and enhancing competence of self through continued professional development (CPD).

skills.detail: Follow health and safety regulations and procedures.
Identify, health and safety risks to safe working practices.
Comply with environmental and sustainability regulations, standards and guidance.
Apply sustainable principles and techniques.
Comply with engineering regulations, legislation, codes, policies, standards and strategies.
Assist in applying engineering principles by using established and emerging technologies.
Plan and prioritise own work in line with agreed time allowances.
Prepare schedules and reports, for example quantity take offs.
Recognise limitations of their role, seek input from others and escalate issues when required.
Use information technology and digital systems. Comply with GDPR and cyber security regulations and policies.
Apply quality assurance procedures and monitoring processes of your own work within the digital asset.
Manage and comply with objectives, requirements and value including Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key performance indicators (KPI’s).
Work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders and as part of a team.
Communicate with internal and external stakeholders using sector specific terminology through verbal and written means.
Analyse and report different types of data according to its qualities.
Input to the development of a BIM execution plan (BEP) and capability and capacity assessments.
Federate building information model and carry out clash detection.
Apply techniques to carry out digital information model checks and data validation.
Apply the principles and practices of a common data environment (CDE).
Produce 3D modelling as required within an organisational project In line with BEP requirements.
Apply problem solving techniques, identifying issues. Propose solutions to problems.
Extract and interpret information from sources.
Apply and promote policies and practices to support equity, diversity and inclusion.
Plan and undertake Continued Professional Development (CPD) to meet personal and organisational development. Evaluate CPD outcomes against any plans made.

clusterDescription: Design, analyse, plan for site engineering and construction projects. Specialisms are common (e.g. rail infrastructure, asbestos management). Significant capability in the use of IT/digital technology, data collection, analysis and presentation

duties.dutyDetail: Comply with health and safety legislation and obligations along with organisational requirements, to protect your and others health, safety and wellbeing.
Comply with all relevant industry standards, legislation, compliance obligations, and organisational policies, plans and processes.
Promote sustainable practices and minimise environmental impact in digital engineering operations.
Plan, organise and manage digital engineering activities in ways which use resources in consideration of cost, quality, time, safety, security and society.
Use quality and information management and assurance systems and processes, for example BS EN ISO 19650, recognising the need for these and their role in continuous improvement.
Develop project information models, evaluate the quality of the generated data, and report any discrepancies.
Collect, analyse and interpret data to produce and coordinate digital models using industry specific software and tools.
Support the implementation of model coordination and mobilisation plans.
Organising, measuring and managing project data throughout the life cycle.
Contribute to delivering activities and projects in support of the organisation’s digital strategies.
Integrate technology and innovation throughout the lifecycle of the project.
Maintain information records utilising the relevant standards and technology.
Work collaboratively and support others to meet stakeholder and quality requirements.
